issues.legal_issue: A consent decree based on a compromise that is not vitiated by fraud, misrepresentation, misunderstanding, or mistake binds the parties and prevents relitigation of the matter it resolved.
material_facts: An earlier partition suit sought division of all family property and determination of accounts for the family businesses.
The parties agreed that accounts would be taken only up to a specified cutoff date, although they knew that businesses might continue afterward.
The compromise and resulting decree did not provide for reopening accounts for the later period.
The compromise was not vitiated by fraud, misrepresentation, misunderstanding, or mistake.
A later suit sought accounts for the motor business for a period beyond the cutoff.
issues.conclusion: The consent decree finally closed the controversy over accounts for the later period, and the later claim was barred by res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: A consent decree is as binding on its parties as a decree passed after contest. If the compromise underlying it is not vitiated by fraud, misrepresentation, misunderstanding, or mistake, the decree has the binding force of res judicata as to the matter resolved. No earlier case was relied on for this principle.

rule.if: consent_decree_case and prior_suit_included_business_accounts and prior_decree_set_accounting_cutoff and later_claim_reopens_accounting_beyond_cutoff and compromise_free_of_vitiating_defect

predicates.consent_decree_case: The later proceeding seeks relief concerning a matter addressed in an earlier proceeding resolved by consent decree.
predicates.prior_suit_included_business_accounts: The claimant included accounts for the relevant businesses in the claims made in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_decree_set_accounting_cutoff: The parties agreed, and the decree provided, that accounting would end at a specified cutoff.
predicates.later_claim_reopens_accounting_beyond_cu: The claimant later sought accounts for a period beyond the cutoff fixed in the earlier decree.
predicates.compromise_free_of_vitiating_defect: The compromise was not affected by fraud, misrepresentation, misunderstanding, or mistake.

issues.definition: When a later claim in a consent-decree case seeks to reopen business accounting that the earlier decree included and limited to a cutoff, and the compromise was not vitiated by a specified defect, the later claim is barred by res judicata.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who omits relief available on the same cause of action in an earlier suit, without leave to omit it, cannot seek that relief in a later suit.
material_facts: The earlier partition suit sought division of all family property and determination of the family business accounts.
The claimant limited the accounting relief in the earlier suit to a specified cutoff and did not seek accounts for the later period.
The claimant later sued for accounts for the motor business for that later period.
The later claim arose from the same desire to separate and divide the family property that formed the basis of the earlier suit.
The claimant had no leave of the court to omit the later-period accounting relief.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was barred under Order II, rule 2(3), of the Code of Civil Procedure because the omitted relief arose from the same cause of action.
issues.legal_principle: Order II, rule 2(3), of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that a person who omits, without the court’s leave, relief to which that person is entitled cannot later sue for the omitted relief. The Court held that the cause of action in the later suit was the same as in the earlier partition suit.

rule.if: later_suit_after_prior_partition_suit and same_separation_cause and relief_omitted_from_prior_suit and no_leave_to_omit_relief

predicates.later_suit_after_prior_partition_suit: The claimant brought a later suit after an earlier suit seeking partition of shared family property.
predicates.same_separation_cause: The earlier and later suits arose from the claimant’s wish to separate and divide the shared family property.
predicates.relief_omitted_from_prior_suit: The claimant did not seek in the earlier suit relief that was later sought in the subsequent suit.
predicates.no_leave_to_omit_relief: The claimant had not obtained the court’s permission to omit that relief from the earlier suit.

issues.definition: When a later suit follows a partition suit, arises from the same separation cause, seeks relief omitted from the earlier suit, and the claimant had no leave to omit it, the later claim is barred as omitted relief.
